title: observability: token-kv cost/latency dashboard and alert refinements
author: Ava Chen
description: Motivation: reduce noisy alerts and provide clearer token-level KV cache cost and latency breakdowns used by infra and product teams. This PR refines dashboards, tightens alert thresholds, adds new token-level KV metrics and tracing spans, and templates dashboards by model+route to make triage faster. Changes include: new metrics token_kv_cache_hit_rate, token_processing_latency_ms_{p50,p90,p99}, token_kv_extra_cost_per_token, instrumented KV lookup span with route/model tags, dashboard layout updates, and updated Prometheus alerting rules to reduce false positives during bursty workloads. Includes migration notes for teams and a short runbook pointer. Checklist: 1) implement metrics and traces 2) update dashboards and templates 3) tune alerts and add grace windows 4) add unit + integration tests for metric labels 5) update docs and runbook 6) validate with dashboard-lint and CI. Context: last month we had repeated paging noise from TOKEN_KV_COST spikes during scheduled model refreshes (incident SUP-213). Prometheus rules were too sensitive to p99 short-lived spikes and lacked route/model labels, which made ownership ambiguous. This work came from ENG-3472 and SRE-1145 to add token-level breakdowns, KV-specific hit/miss metrics, and more robust alerting. Impact: improved alert precision, faster owner identification, and richer dashboards for cost/latency attribution.

review_comments: Diego Ramos: Nice work on the metrics; a couple of questions: can we avoid cardinality explosion from route/model labels? Suggest limiting model label to canonical model family.

Ava Chen: Reply: agreed; implemented a canonical_model label and a mapping function in token_metrics.go to map variants to family names. Kept full model id as audit label but not high-cardinality in Prometheus metrics.
Priya Kapoor: Alert thresholds look better but p99 over short windows can still spike; can we add a saturating moving average or require sustained signal?

Ava Chen: Reply: implemented a 5m grace window and moved the expression to use increase() over 5m for cost and avg_over_time for latency to require sustained elevation. Also added a secondary alert for short-lived p99 spikes routed to a quieter channel.
Liam O'Neill: Please add tests for label preservation through the ingestion pipeline and a note in the runbook about known caveats during model rollouts.
Ava Chen: Added tests and runbook note. Fixed a flake in metrics test discovered during CI run.
release_notes: Refined token-level KV dashboards and tuned alerts to reduce noise and improve cost/latency attribution. Added token_kv_cache_hit_rate and p50/p90/p99 latency metrics, tracing for KV lookups, and templated dashboards by model+route. Upgrade requires running the provided migration script and noting the new canonical_model label in queries.
